children.translated_text: How, O Lord, [is attained] the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>), which of itself grants <s>Kaulika</s> attainment,
by the mere knowledge of which one reaches equality with the <s>Khecarī</s>s (sky-moving goddesses)? (1)

children.text: etad guhyaṃ mahāguhyaṃ kathayasva mama prabho |
children.translated_text: Tell me this secret, the great secret, O my Lord!

children.text: hṛdayasthā tu yā śaktiḥ kaulinī kulanāyikā || 2 ||
children.translated_text: The power (<s>Śakti</s>) that dwells in the heart, the <s>Kaulinī</s>, the mistress of the <s>Kula</s> — (2)

body.text: tām me kathaya deveśa yena tṛptiṃ vrajāmy aham |
body.translated_text: tell me of her, O Lord of Gods, by which I may attain satisfaction!
Listen, O Goddess, O greatly fortunate one, to that which is the unsurpassed even of the supreme! (3)

children.translated_text: I shall tell [you], without doubt, that which at once grants <s>Kaulika</s> attainment.

children.text: kauliko 'yaṃ vidhir devi mama hṛdvyomny avasthitaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Kaulika</s> procedure, O Goddess, abides in the space of my heart. (4)
Now, all the initial <s>tithi</s>s (lunar days) [are] the vowels, ending with the <s>bindu</s> (dot);
within these, by the conjunction of time, the Moon (<s>Soma</s>) and the Sun (<s>Sūrya</s>) are proclaimed. (5)
The principles (<s>tattva</s>) beginning with earth, up to <s>Puruṣa</s>, [are distributed] among the five
[consonant] groups beginning with KA and ending with MA, O lady of good vows! (6)
The four concentrations (<s>dhāraṇā</s>) of wind, fire, water, and <s>Indra</s>;
above that, the well-known [group] beginning with ŚA, and before that, the fivefold <s>Brahman</s>. (7)

children.text: amūlā tatkramā jñeyā kṣāntā sṛṣṭir udāhṛtā |
children.translated_text: The rootless [letters], known in that order, ending with KṢA — [this] is declared as the emanation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>)

children.text: sarveṣāṃ caiva mantrāṇāṃ vidyānāṃ ca yaśasvini || 8 ||
children.translated_text: of all mantras and <s>vidyā</s>s, O illustrious one! (8)
This is proclaimed as the womb (<s>yoni</s>) in all tantras, always.
Combined with the fourteen, O auspicious one, accompanied by the <s>tithi</s>-lord and the end [phoneme],
the third [level of] <s>Brahman</s>, O fair-hipped one, is the heart of <s>Bhairava</s> himself. (9)

children.text: etan nā yoginījāto nā rudro labhate sphuṭam |
children.translated_text: This — neither one born of <s>Yoginī</s>s nor a <s>Rudra</s> obtains clearly
the heart of the God of Gods, which at once grants yoga and liberation. (10)
When this is properly uttered, the great host of mantra-<s>mudrā</s>s
at once becomes favorable, characterized by possession (<s>āveśa</s>) of one's own body. (11)

children.text: muhūrtaṃ smarate yas tu cumbake nābhimudritaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who remembers for [even] a moment, sealed in the <s>cumbaka</s> [kiss-method], at the navel —

children.text: sa badhnāti tadā dehaṃ mantramudrāgaṇaṃ naraḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: that person then binds the body [and] the host of mantra-<s>mudrā</s>s. (12)
Asked, he tells of past and future events;
within a <s>prahara</s> (three hours), uttering the desired deity's form, (13)
he directly sees, without doubt, [that deity] drawn by the powers of <s>Rudra</s>;
within two <s>prahara</s>s, remembering, he becomes situated in the sky. (14)
Within three, all the Mothers, the great and mighty <s>Yogeśvarī</s>s,
the <s>Vīra</s>s, the <s>Vīreśvara</s>s, the <s>Siddha</s>s, and the powerful host of <s>Śākinī</s>s — (15)
having come and given [their] pledge, impelled by <s>Bhairava</s>,

children.text: yacchanti paramāṃ siddhiṃ phalaṃ yad vā samīhitam || 16 ||
children.translated_text: they grant the supreme attainment, or whatever fruit is desired. (16)

body.text: anena siddhāḥ setsyanti sādhayanti ca mantriṇaḥ || 17 ||
body.translated_text: By this, the accomplished ones have attained and will attain perfection, and the <s>mantrin</s>s accomplish [all goals]. (17)

children.text: yatkiṃcid bhairave tantre sarvam asmāt prasidhyati |
children.translated_text: Whatever is in the <s>Bhairava</s> tantra, everything is accomplished from this.
By the power of the absorption of mantra-force — not by one who is [merely] restrained. (18)

children.text: adṛṣṭama.ṅdalo 'py evam yaḥ kaścid vetti tattvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Even one without the [proper] circle of ritual, whoever knows this in truth,

children.text: sa siddhibhāg bhaven nityaṃ sa yogī sa ca dīkṣītaḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: becomes a partaker of attainment perpetually; he is a yogin, he is an initiate. (19)
By the mere knowing of this, one is known by all the <s>Śakti</s>s;
one becomes equal to the clan of <s>Śākinī</s>s, even without [formal] yoga! (20)
One ignorant of [proper] procedure becomes a knower of procedure with regard to worship.
Beginning with <s>Kālāgni</s> [and proceeding] up to <s>Māyā</s>, [placing these] in the body of <s>Brahman</s> — (21)
<s>Śiva</s>, from the universe up to <s>Ananta</s>, is considered the supreme triad of powers;
whatever exists within that, established on the pure path — (22)

children.text: aṇur viśuddham acirād aisvaraṃ jñānam aśnute |
children.translated_text: the individual soul (<s>aṇu</s>) swiftly attains the pure, sovereign knowledge (<s>aiśvara jñāna</s>);
the impeller of that should be known as <s>Śiva</s>, the omniscient Supreme Lord. (23)

children.text: sarvago nirmalaḥ svacchas tṛptaḥ svāyatanaḥ śuciḥ |
children.translated_text: All-pervading, stainless, transparent, satisfied, self-abiding, pure;
just as a great tree exists in potential form within the seed of the banyan — (24)
so this world of moving and unmoving [beings] abides within the seed of the heart.

children.text: evaṃ yo vetti tattvena tasya nirvāṇagāminī || 25 ||
children.translated_text: One who knows this in truth — for him, [there is] the initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, (25)
which comes about without doubt, without oblations of sesame and ghee.

children.text: mūrdhni vaktre ca hṛdaye guhye murtau tathaiva ca || 26 ||
children.translated_text: On the crown, the face, the heart, the secret [organ], and the body — (26)
having performed the <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) and tied the topknot, consecrated with twenty-seven [mantras],

children.text: ekaikena diśāṃ bandhaṃ daśānām api kārayet || 27 ||
children.translated_text: one should have the binding of the ten directions performed, one by one. (27)
Having first given three claps with sound, for the pacification of obstacles,
one should then sprinkle with water recited over the number of the topknot [mantras]. (28)

children.text: puṣpādikaṃ kramāt sarvaṃ liṅgaṃ vā stha.ṅdilaṃ ca vā |
children.translated_text: All [offerings of] flowers and the rest, in sequence — whether on a <s>liṅga</s> or on a ground-altar,
with a flower recited over fourteen [times], the preparation of the seat [is done]. (29)

children.text: tatra sṛṣṭiṃ yajed vīraḥ punar evāsanaṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: There the hero should worship the emanation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>), then the seat again;

children.text: sṛṣṭiṃ tu sampuṭīkṛtya paścād yajanam ārabhet || 30 ||
children.translated_text: Having enclosed the <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (emanation) in a <s>sampuṭa</s> (sealed container), one should then commence the worship. // 30 //
Completely filled with all <s>tattvas</s> (principles), adorned with all limbs,
One should worship the <s>Devī</s> (Goddess), the greatly fortunate one, consecrated with twenty-seven <s>mantras</s>. // 31 //
Then, with fragrant flowers, one should worship to the best of one's ability;

children.text: pūjayet parayā bhaktyā svātmanaṃ ca nivedayet || 32 ||
children.translated_text: One should worship with supreme devotion and offer one's own self. // 32 //

children.text: evaṃ yajanam ākhyātam agnikārye 'py ayaṃ vidhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus the worship has been declared; this same procedure applies to the fire ritual as well.
Having properly performed the rite of worship, one who meditates on the <s>bīja</s> (seed-syllable) attains perfection. // 33 //
The <s>bīja</s> (seed-syllable), devoid of beginning and end, blossoming, situated in the middle of the <s>tithi</s> (lunar day),
One should meditate upon it within the lotus of the heart; one should constantly practice the <s>somāṃśu</s> (lunar ray). // 34 //

children.text: yān yān kāmayate kāmāṃs tān tāñ cchīghram avāpnuyāt |
children.translated_text: Whatever desires one desires, those one quickly attains;

children.text: ajñaḥ pratyakṣatām eti sarvajñatvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ || 35 ||
children.translated_text: The ignorant one attains direct perception; omniscience is attained without doubt. // 35 //
Thus the attainment of the fruit of <s>mantra</s> — this is the <s>Rudrayāmala</s>.
Through the practice of this, <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) and omniscience are attained. // 36 //
